title: Babur resolves to seek Guru Nanak's grace

blocks.text: Babur's despair begins to clear when he remembers that even Muhammad acknowledged Guru Nanak as the true spiritual authority for India. That recognition convinces him that his only hope is to fall at Guru Nanak's feet and beg directly for mercy.

He therefore turns to Daulat Khan and asks him to help arrange an approach to the Guru. Babur abandons royal pride, returns in humility, and prepares himself to speak not as a conqueror but as a supplicant.

The page closes in a mood of reverence, with Babur praising Guru Nanak's unmatched nearness to the Divine and presenting himself as the servant of the Guru's servants. What began as political ambition is now recast as an appeal for grace.
